content:
maya: Paging — noticed a steady rise in CUDA OOMs on us-west-2-serving-3 around 09:03 UTC. Containers are restarting; 5 restarts in 8m. Root trace shows paged-attention allocator hitting fragmented allocations, slow vertex of leak. PD: P123456.

ops-bot: Incident P123456 created by maya. Severity: Sev2. Affected: hosted-inference/us-west-2, subset of dedicated nodes.

toni: Oncall taking this. quick checks: are we seeing the KV cache grow unbounded or fragmentation in the slab allocator?

maya: Obs so far: per-container RSS creeping from 6.2GB -> 11.3GB over ~30m for some long-lived sessions. CPU ok. GPU memory shows spikes then OOMs. suspect paged-attn eviction pressure + small alloc churn.

leo: @toni fyi I saw similar pattern last week but it resolved after slab-defrag task. This looks like slow-drip fragmentation not a one-off big leak. Could be race in paged allocator refill path.

sam: Can we hot-fix by lowering max_seq_len for heavy routes, or reduce per-request kv_cache retention TTL? Thinking quick config rollback to reduce steady-state KV size.

toni: Agreed. Plan: 1) temporarily reduce kv_cache_ttl from 60m -> 5m for hosted inference in us-west-2. 2) Enable aggressive per-shard eviction (evict_threshold -> 0.6). 3) Roll a small canary of rollback on 10% traffic. If stable, roll to 100%.

june: Patching config now, starting canary on pool us-west-2-serving-3-canal. Will annotate rollout.

ops-bot: Deploy started: config-change/kv_ttl_shortened by june. Canary target: us-west-2-serving-3-canal (10%).

maya: While canary rolls, attaching recent logs from one container that OOMed:

```
[2026-03-10T09:02:58Z] serve: request id=abc123 start seq=1024
[2026-03-10T09:03:12Z] allocator: paged_alloc slab id=12 alloc_size=32768 -> returned ptr
[2026-03-10T09:05:41Z] kvcache: insert key=conv:xyz size=2.1MB total_cached=3.8GB
[2026-03-10T09:08:05Z] cuda: <warning> memory fragmentation high: free blocks 128, avg_block=32MB
[2026-03-10T09:10:21Z] runtime: caught cudaErrorOutOfMemory
[2026-03-10T09:10:21Z] container: restarting due to OOM (exit code 137)
```

leo: That avg_block line looks like fragmentation - many mid-sized free blocks but none big enough for large attention windows. Causes paging behavior and OOMs when attention needs contiguous slab.

toni: Canary shows initial improvement: canary containers' RSS growth flattened after kv_ttl change. No OOMs in last 6m on canary. I'm going to expand to 30% traffic in 5m and monitor.

sam: Customer impact status? Any API error spikes / 5xxs?

maya: Metrics summary: 5xxs up 0.6% overall for hosted inference us-west-2 during incident window, peak p50 latency +30ms. A small set of customers on heavy long-context workloads saw transient failures (~20 unique API keys). Logged and will notify CS.

june: Rolling to 30% now. Ops dashboard: https://dash.redwood/incident/P123456

ops-bot: Rollout to 30% complete. No new OOM alerts on canary nodes.

toni: Good sign. Next step: run targeted defrag job on idling nodes during off-peak. Will schedule background slab-defrag v2 that compacts paged-attn free lists. ETA 20m.

leo: Defrag job command (dry-run):
```
./scripts/defrag_paged_attn.sh --pool us-west-2-serving-3 --dry-run
# will iterate shards, coalesce free spans, write metrics to /tmp/defrag.log
```

maya: Also adding temporary fallback model routing: if a request would allocate >X MB contiguous then route to quantized-variant (less mem). Quick config is in feature flags. That should reduce incidence of big alloc failures.

sam: Noted. I'll notify product/CS which customers hit errors so support can reach out.

june: Defrag dry-run shows coalesce rate 82% and predicted reclaimed ~1.9GB per node. Scheduling non-dry run in 10m with low-priority nice.

ops-bot: Background job scheduled: defrag_paged_attn/us-west-2-serving-3 at 09:42 UTC.

maya: Handing off to next oncall in ~30m. Current state: kv_ttl shortened (canary 30%), aggressive eviction on, fallback routing enabled. Observable signs: OOM rate down from 4.3/min -> 0.4/min across pool. Customer impact reduced to transient errors; SLOs degraded for a small segment.

toni: Handoff notes for next oncall (leo): keep eviction at 0.6 until defrag completes and we see 15m stabilization. If OOMs spike again, revert rollback and scale pool + trigger full node drain for thorough defrag and kernel logs collection.

leo: Got it. I'll monitor for the next hour. If we see OOM >1/min for 3 consecutive minutes, escalate to Sev1 and we'll start node drains.

pagerduty-bot: Handoff to leo acknowledged. Next oncall: leo.

maya: Thanks team. I'll update the incident doc with timeline and customer list, and draft initial postmortem stub.

sam: Adding customer notification draft to #support-alerts.

leo: Taking over. thumbs up. :thumbsup:

june: leaving a note: upload /tmp/defrag.log and one sample container core dump to /incidents/P123456/artifacts.

ops-bot: Incident P123456 status: mitigation in progress, monitoring.

maya: closing thread — leaving final comment here for context for whoever picks up.

maya: tl;dr — slow paged-attn fragmentation causing memory creep -> CUDA OOMs. Mitigations: short-term kv_ttl + aggressive eviction + fallback routing + background defrag. Monitoring & follow-up: full postmortem + fix in allocator refill path.
